items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: As well as he and I got along, you know, I say he's going to bring me the bill... he threw his arms around my shoulder... and thanked me for tearing up the club

ctx.x: I mean last year when you told me about it.

No, no, no. No, not under scale, never. No, I always got over scale. I wasn't a scale musician. I never worked for scales in Chicago. Only time that I worked for scales in Chicago, in New York was Stuff Smith, my first job. And then little by little as I felt my worth, you know if they wanted me, I asked my price. If they just wanted a bass player, they'd go get someone else. This is how I found out what my worth was. Sometimes, I under played myself, you know and other times I over-rated myself too, you know.…

But, I went to court. And he won his suit. He said after we got outside, if anyone ask you what happened, just tell them it's a misunderstanding. He says come on over to the house and have a drink. Now, you know, I'm pouting like mad, I'm ready to blow up like a blimp, you know. I said all right. I go over to his house. He said what are you drinking? I say a glass of water, I'm afraid he going to give me a Mickey Finn, anything to get even, you know. But I didn't tell you the aftermath, after the fight.
